newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil airplane blast was caused by bomb - Globo.
newsitem.headline: Brazil airplane blast was caused by bomb - Globo.

text.p: A Brazilian airliner explosion which blew a passenger out of the aircraft in mid-flight was caused by a bomb placed underneath one of the plane's seats, Globo television reported on Monday night.
A report by the Technical Air and Space Centre, not yet made public, said the bomb consisted of about 7 ounces (200 grams) of ammonium nitrate wrapped in newspaper, Globo said.
Police still do not know who was responsible for planting the device on Brazilian airline TAM's flight 283, Globo added.
The Technical Air and Space Centre declined to confirm the report, and said it did not yet know when it would make the results of its investigation public.
"We can't confirm the information they put out," a spokesman for the centre told Reuters on Tuesday. "Our work continues and we are still investigating."

The Fokker-100 was on a routine flight between Sao Jose dos Campos, an industrial city 70 miles (110 km) west of Sao Paulo, and Sao Paulo's domestic Congonhas airport on July 9 when the blast occurred.

The explosion tore a six-foot by four-foot (two metres by 1.3-metres) hole in the fuselage and a 38-year-old engineer plunged 7,200 feet (2,400 metres) to his death. The body of Fernando Caldeira de Moura Campos was found next to parts of the airplane in a field outside the town of Suzano, 30 miles (50 km) from Sao Paulo's domestic Congonhas airport.
The airplane made an emergency landing at Congonhas shortly after and no one else was injured.
A 14-ounce (400-gram) dose of ammonium nitrate would have been sufficient to break the plane in two, which would probably have killed all 60 passengers on board, Globo said.
